title: Epoch-based progressive rollout with safety envelopes and auto-rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Implement an epoch-based progressive delivery mechanism that advances traffic in discrete epochs (time-boxed windows) with per-epoch safety envelopes and automated rollback when health regressions exceed configurable thresholds. This will be the primary rollout primitive for runtime-1.20 and the basis for future LTS channel upgrades.

Background: Current rollouts are percent-based ramps but lack a clear bounded epoch construct and tight safety envelopes. This leads to slow detection of regressions and noisy rollback behavior. An epoch-based approach gives clearer windows for evaluation and deterministic advancement logic tied to metrics.

Scope:
- Core rollout controller that implements epochs, epoch-level metrics aggregation, and advancement policies.
- Safety envelopes: per-epoch thresholds for error rate, latency p50/p95/p99, token failure rate, and model quality regression signals (from eval hooks).
- Auto-rollback: deterministic rollback when a safety envelope breach persists for the configured epoch(s).
- Feature flag integration so a rollout can be gated by a flag targeting cohorts or tenant groups.
- LTS channel fallback: when rollback occurs for a non-LTS release, optionally pin affected tenants to the previous LTS channel until investigation completes.
- Observability: dashboards and SLO checks for epoch outcomes and rollout health.

Acceptance criteria:
- New controller can enact epoched ramps (e.g., epochs of 10 minutes advancing 5% traffic each epoch) via API and console.
- Safety envelopes are configurable per rollout and enforced automatically.
- Auto-rollback triggers within one epoch after persistent envelope breach according to policy.
- Rollout history shows epoch-level metrics and decision rationale in the Console.
- Unit + integration tests exercising advancement, rollback, and LTS fallback paths.
- Playbook and runbook for on-call to override rollouts and inspect epoch data.
design_decisions:
1) Epoch length default: 10 minutes. Chosen as a balance between signal accumulation and time-to-rollback for latency-sensitive workloads.
2) Aggregation window: use epoch-aligned aggregation (no sliding windows) so advancement == discrete evaluation.
3) Safety envelopes: use relative and absolute thresholds. Start with absolute thresholds for latency and error-rate, add relative (percent change vs baseline) for quality signals.
4) Auto-rollback staleness: require breach for 1 full epoch by default; optional 'grace_epochs' configurable per rollout.
5) LTS fallback: implement as optional policy per customer. Default behavior: revert traffic to previous pinned model variant; for Dedicated/Private tenants, expose toggle for immediate rollback or delayed investigation.
6) Feature flagging: leverage existing flags service; rollout controller treats flags as prefilters for cohorts and applies epochs only to the flagged subset.
implementation_plan:
Milestone 1 (week 1-2): Controller skeleton, API schema, and simple epoch timer. Create REST endpoints and Console UI placeholders.
Milestone 2 (week 3): Safety envelope evaluation engine (error-rate, latency buckets) and epoch aggregation pipeline.
Milestone 3 (week 4): Auto-rollback action plumbing (traffic shift, model pinning). Integrate feature-flagging paths.
Milestone 4 (week 5): LTS fallback integration and tenant-level overrides.
Milestone 5 (week 6): End-to-end tests, chaos testing for false positives, and Console telemetry.
Deploy plan: feature-flag the controller behind "epoch-rollout" flag initially for internal teams. Gradually enable for a small set of customers, then open it to all.
Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-controller/pull/212 (skeleton) ; https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/98 (epoch metrics).
test_plan:
Unit tests for epoch timer and aggregation.
Integration tests simulating traffic (synthetic load with injected latency/error).
Canary experiments: run controller in dry-run mode for 48 hours against production traffic to surface false positives.
Chaos scenarios: mid-epoch cluster flapping, delayed metrics ingestion, and partial telemetry loss. Verify rollback behavior is deterministic and safe.
Load testing: validate controller scales to 10k concurrent rollouts with sharded state.
Security: ensure rollback actions are audited and require a signed request for manual overrides.
rollout_plan:
Default rollout profile: epochs of 10 minutes, advance 5% per epoch up to 50%, then 10% increments to 100% with a 30-minute stabilization window post-100%.
Safety envelope defaults: error-rate < 0.5% absolute; latency p95 < baseline + 150ms; model-eval-quality delta < -1.5% (relative).
Auto-rollback policy: immediate rollback if safety envelope breached for 1 epoch; if "grace_epochs"=2 then rollback requires breach across 2 consecutive epochs.
Manual override: on-call can pause or force-advance via Console. Any manual action must include a justification and will be audited.
LTS fallback: when enabled, rollback will route affected tenants to the most recent LTS model variant instead of the immediate previous canary variant.
Communication: the Console will post rollout status to #deployments channel with epoch summaries and links to epoch dashboards.
metrics_and_alerts:
Primary metrics: per-epoch error_rate, latency_p50/p95/p99, token_failure_rate, model_quality_eval_score, traffic_percent.
Derived signals: relative change vs baseline (1h baseline) and long-tail spike detectors.
Alert rules: page on error_rate > 1.5x baseline AND absolute > 1.0% for two epochs, or latency p99 > baseline + 300ms.
Auto-rollback triggers: configured safety envelope breach AND epoch persistence (default 1).
Non-blocking alerts: notify Slack when minor regressions are detected but below rollback thresholds.
All alerts include epoch_id, rollout_id, and links to raw logs and traces.
